local function equal(actual, expected, label)
	checks = checks + 1
	if actual ~= expected then
		error(("%s: expected %s, got %s"):format(label, tostring(expected), tostring(actual)), 2)
	end
end

No canonical home exists; tests/ui_helpers.lua is the one shared helper module and holds only Button and FindText.

A fix to the failure message or to table comparison lands in one spec. Low confidence because each spec is a standalone luajit script with its own counter and the body is short, which may put it under the small-idiom exclusion.
items.reason: The assertion preamble (checks counter, equal, same, clean) is retyped in 18 spec files and `same` has drifted (keyed Flat in tests/ui_spec.lua, table.concat only in asides, moments, guide_ui and tooltip specs). items.why: rg 'runtime_files' tools returns exactly these two definitions and four callers, so the four gate lints disagree on what the runtime set is. Differences: the lint_multivalue copy globs only root-level *.toc, keeps only lines ending .lua, never checks the file exists and does not follow XML; the typecheck_coverage copy rglobs TOCs (child addons), follows <Include>/<Script file=> in listed XML, raises on a missing file and on runtime Lua no TOC loads, and returns resolved paths. That is accidental drift, not a stated divergence: the TOC lists UI\Panel.xml, which has no <Script file> today (grep returned none), so results match now, but a Lua file loaded from XML or a child TOC would be covered by the taint lint and LuaLS coverage and silently skipped by the multi-value and copy lints. Check when merging: lint_copy filters on p.parent.name != "Data" and the lints pass a root derived from __file__, while typecheck_coverage's callers pass Path.cwd().

items.what: lint_multivalue.py holds two responsibilities: the shared Lua tokenizer (Token, TokenKind, LuaSyntaxError, tokenize, lines 14-89), imported by tools/lint_copy.py:7, tools/lint_taint.py:12 and tools/lint_copy_test.py:6, and the select() expansion lint itself (PRECEDENCE, Parser, check, main, lines 92-345), used only by its own CLI and test.
items.why: The tokenizer changes for reasons the select() lint does not share (lint_copy needs string and long-bracket tokens, lint_taint needs the comment map), yet every such change edits the multi-value lint's file, and two other linters depend on a module named for one rule. The two parts separate cleanly: the tokenizer block would live in its own module (for example tools/lua_tokens.py) with the three linters importing it one way, which would also remove the `if __package__` double import at lines 9-12. A split is its own reviewed change, not part of an audit.
items.reason: Move the shared Lua tokenizer (Token, TokenKind, LuaSyntaxError, tokenize) out of tools/lint_multivalue.py into its own module? lint_copy.py, lint_taint.py, phrases.py and lint_copy_test.py import it from a module named for one rule, and the `if __package__` import exists only because lint_taint imports it as tools.lint_multivalue.

items.quote: kind: str = "symbol"
items.what: Token.kind is a closed set of five values (symbol, name, keyword, number, string) typed as bare str and compared by literal in four files; type it as a Literal or Enum defined beside Token.
items.why: rg 'kind (==|!=|in)' tools finds 20 literal comparisons: lint_multivalue.py:128,172,197,199,227, lint_copy.py:57,59,72,77,98,109,119,127, lint_taint.py:53,68,78,104,114,118, phrases.py:39; the set is produced only in tokenize (lint_multivalue.py:68-78). A misspelt kind at any read site is a comparison that is always false, which for these lints means a rule that silently passes; nothing enumerates the set and ruff's selected rules (E,F,I,UP,B) cannot catch it. screenshots.py solved the same problem for its phases with a PHASES tuple and a test; the lints have no equivalent.

items.quote: paths = [Path(arg) for arg in sys.argv[1:]] or runtime_files(Path.cwd().resolve())
items.what: Three copies of the Lua lint command-line driver: tools/lint_taint.py:151-164, tools/lint_multivalue.py:326-341 and tools/lint_copy.py:143-150. Each takes optional file arguments, defaults to runtime_files(root), reads and tokenizes each file, prints path:line hits and returns 1 on any hit. Canonical home: lint_multivalue.py (argparse, root from __file__), which already owns the shared tokenizer.
items.why: Drift between the copies, none with a stated reason: lint_taint reads sys.argv and takes the root from Path.cwd(), the other two use argparse and Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent, so lint_taint only works from the repository root; lint_taint prints read and syntax errors to stderr, lint_multivalue to stdout, and lint_copy catches neither (a LuaSyntaxError or missing file is a traceback); lint_taint imports tools.lint_multivalue and is run as python3 -m tools.lint_taint (tools/typecheck.sh:25) while lint_copy imports lint_multivalue and is run as a script (typecheck.sh:27-28), which is why lint_multivalue.py:9-12 carries an `if __package__` double import and why unittest discovery loads the tokenizer module twice under two names (two LuaSyntaxError classes). A change to how the default file set, the root or a read error is handled has to be made three times.
items.reason: Unify the Lua lint command-line drivers (tools/lint_taint.py:151-164, tools/lint_multivalue.py:326-341, part of tools/lint_copy.py:143-150)? They differ in root (lint_taint uses the working directory, so run outside the repository root it finds no TOC, checks nothing and exits 0), error stream and import style, so one driver changes those.
